title: What education and exams do insurance solicitors need in Japan?
description: How Japan's Insurance Business Act registers insurance solicitors and what industry exams, renewal cycles and annual continuing education apply to them.
shortAnswer: In Japan, the Insurance Business Act (保険業法) bars anyone from soliciting insurance unless registered or notified under Articles 275 and 276, and its Enforcement Regulations require insurers and solicitors to train staff. Industry bodies run the exams: life insurance solicitors must pass the Life Insurance Association of Japan's general course exam before registration and complete continuing education every year, and non-life solicitors take the General Insurance Association of Japan's exam on a five year renewal cycle.
keyTakeaways: Article 275 of the Insurance Business Act prohibits insurance solicitation except by registered or otherwise authorized persons, and Article 276 requires specified insurance solicitors to register with the Prime Minister.
Article 227-7 of the Enforcement Regulations requires solicitors and brokers to set internal rules and build systems, including employee training, so business is run under those rules.
Article 53(1)(iii) of the Enforcement Regulations requires insurers to take measures to improve solicitors' ability to solicit fairly.

The Life Insurance Association of Japan requires company training before the general course exam, which must be passed before registration, and has required annual continuing education for, in principle, all life insurance solicitors since 2009.
The General Insurance Association of Japan's non-life solicitor exam has basic and product units and is renewed every five years.
regulator: Financial Services Agency (FSA), exercising the Prime Minister's registration powers through the Local Finance Bureaus, with industry education run by the Life Insurance Association of Japan (LIAJ) and the General Insurance Association of Japan (GIAJ)
appliesTo: Life insurance solicitors (生命保険募集人), including sales staff of life insurers and agency staff
Non-life insurance agents (損害保険代理店) and the solicitors who work in them
Insurers, which must take measures to improve solicitors' ability to solicit fairly
Insurance brokers (保険仲立人), for internal rules and staff training

sections.heading: Who is allowed to solicit insurance in Japan?

blocks.text: Only registered or otherwise authorized persons may solicit insurance. Article 275 of the Insurance Business Act states that, except for the categories it lists, "何人も保険募集を行ってはならない" (no person may carry out insurance solicitation). The listed categories include life insurance solicitors registered under Article 276, officers and employees of non-life insurers, and registered non-life insurance agents and their officers and employees ([Insurance Business Act, e-Gov](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/407AC0000000105)).

Article 276 requires specified insurance solicitors (特定保険募集人), meaning life insurance solicitors, non-life insurance agents and small amount short term insurance solicitors, to register with the Prime Minister. Article 277 sets out the registration application, including the names of the insurers the solicitor represents. The General Insurance Association of Japan explains that agents register with the Local Finance Bureau that covers their location, that people who solicit within an agency are notified to the bureau, and that these procedures normally run through the insurer ([GIAJ, becoming a non-life agent](https://www.sonpo.or.jp/exam/dairiten/tobe/index.html)).

As at November 2026, the Act itself does not specify an exam. The knowledge requirement comes from the duty on insurers and solicitors to maintain sound operations, implemented through industry exams that insurers require before they submit a registration or notification.

sections.heading: What training duties does the law place on insurers and solicitors?

blocks.text: Two articles of the Enforcement Regulations of the Insurance Business Act (保険業法施行規則) create the training duty. Article 53(1)(iii) requires insurers, under Article 100-2 of the Act, to take measures to improve the ability of life and non-life insurance solicitors to carry out fair solicitation (公正な保険募集を行う能力の向上を図るための措置). Article 227-7 requires solicitors and brokers to set internal rules on explaining important matters, understanding customer intentions and preventing crime, and to build systems "including training for employees" (従業員に対する研修その他) so business runs under those rules ([Enforcement Regulations, e-Gov](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/408M50000040005)).

These duties sit beside the operational management duty in Article 294-3 of the Act, under which solicitors must take measures to secure sound and appropriate operation of their solicitation business, such as explaining important matters to customers, handling customer information properly and, for agencies representing several insurers, providing fair product comparisons. Article 294(3) also requires a solicitor to disclose, before soliciting, which insurer it represents and whether it concludes contracts as agent or acts as an intermediary.

Personal information handling by solicitors also falls under the [Act on the Protection of Personal Information](/regulations/japan-appi-employee-training), and anti money laundering duties under the [FSA AML/CFT guidelines](/regulations/japan-fsa-aml-cft-guidelines-training), so a solicitor's training plan usually spans all three.

sections.heading: What does the Life Insurance Association of Japan require of life insurance solicitors?

blocks.text: The Life Insurance Association of Japan (LIAJ, 生命保険協会) runs an industry wide education system with staged course exams and an annual continuing education scheme. The industry established a common solicitor education system in 1974 and today runs the general, specialist, advanced and life insurance university course exams, plus sales qualification exams for variable and foreign currency insurance ([LIAJ education system](https://www.seiho.or.jp/exam/education/)).

items: **Training before the exam:** to become a life insurance solicitor a person must first pass the general course exam (一般課程試験), and must complete the insurer's training before sitting it. Insurer training is a prerequisite for the general, specialist, variable insurance and foreign currency insurance exams, while the advanced and university courses are self study.

**Sequence for sales staff:** for sales staff the sequence runs from joining, through about three months of prescribed basic training, to the general course exam, passing, registration and practical training. Agencies hold a business entrustment briefing before basic training.

**Specialist qualifications:** passing the specialist course exam earns the Life Consultant title. Variable insurance and foreign currency insurance may be sold only by registered solicitors who have passed the specialist exam, met other requirements, passed the relevant sales qualification exam and registered with the LIAJ.

**Annual continuing education:** since 2009, in principle all life insurance solicitors receive continuing education every year, and solicitors are required to complete training run by their insurer or agency annually, with some companies adding knowledge tests ([LIAJ continuing education](https://www.seiho.or.jp/exam/continue/)).

blocks.text: The continuing education curriculum was redesigned in 2009 to focus on customer orientation and legal compliance, with emphasis on compliance, accountability for explanations and after sales service such as claims payment ([LIAJ curriculum](https://www.seiho.or.jp/exam/curriculum/)).

sections.heading: What exams apply to non-life insurance agents and solicitors?

blocks.text: Non-life agents and their solicitors take the General Insurance Association of Japan's general exam for non-life insurance solicitors (損害保険募集人一般試験), which most non-life insurers use as their agent exam. The GIAJ (日本損害保険協会) describes it as an industry common exam that teaches the knowledge needed to explain important product matters accurately. It has a basic unit (基礎単位) and product units (商品単位) and runs on a five year renewal cycle.

The GIAJ sets out the route: choose the insurer to represent, complete that insurer's agent training, pass the insurer's agent exam, sign an agency entrustment contract, then register with the Local Finance Bureau. It notes that insurers require prior education, such as passing the GIAJ exam, before registering an agent or notifying a solicitor ([GIAJ, about non-life agents](https://www.sonpo.or.jp/exam/dairiten/about/index.html)). The exam is open to people about to register or be notified and to those already registered, with insurer approval.

blocks.text: The Financial Services Agency (FSA) supervises insurers and solicitors on whether their training systems actually work, so evidence should show both exam status and ongoing training. sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry structures the statutory duties, the LIAJ and GIAJ exam units and each insurer's product knowledge as one framework linked to solicitor roles. Annual continuing education content and five year renewals are tracked against that framework, so an insurer can show which solicitors are cleared for which products and when each qualification expires.

faqs.q: Is there a government exam for insurance solicitors in Japan?
faqs.a: No government exam is set in the Insurance Business Act. The Act requires registration or notification and imposes training duties on insurers and solicitors. Knowledge is tested through industry exams run by the Life Insurance Association of Japan and the General Insurance Association of Japan, which insurers require before registration.

faqs.q: Do life insurance solicitors need training every year?
faqs.a: Yes, under the industry scheme. The Life Insurance Association of Japan states that solicitors are required to complete training run by their insurer or agency every year through its continuing education system, introduced in 2009 for, in principle, all life insurance solicitors.

faqs.q: How long is the non-life insurance solicitor exam valid?
faqs.a: The General Insurance Association of Japan's general exam for non-life insurance solicitors runs on a five year renewal system. Agencies should track each solicitor's pass date for the basic unit and each product unit and schedule renewal before expiry.

faqs.q: Can a bank employee sell insurance in Japan?
faqs.a: Banks and their officers or employees can solicit as life insurance solicitors or non-life agents only within the limits of Article 275 and the related Cabinet Office Order, which restricts them to cases where policyholder protection is unlikely to be harmed. They must be registered or notified like other solicitors.
